messages:
Alin: Quick follow-up on the kernel autotuner RFC — I sketched a small proof-of-concept that switches from fixed-length buckets to percentile-based buckets + an optional cache-prefill step. Thinking: percentile bucketing to adapt to long-tail seq distributions, and prefill KV cache for common prefixes to reduce first-token latency. Thoughts?

Sam: curious — how much extra memory does prefill need? prefill could blow GPU mem if we’re not careful.

Maya: agree with Sam. Also need to verify prefill plays nicely with quantized kernels (q4/q8). Some kernels do different workspace allocations.

dev-bot: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/kernel-autotune-2026 (updated section: percentile bucketing + prefill) :link: :eyes:

Ron: did quick numbers on a small model (chrysalis-7b). Percentile buckets (p50,p75,p90,p95,p99) reduced tail latency by ~12% for mixed seq workloads vs fixed 128/256/512 split. Prefill reduced median first-token by ~20ms but consumed ~150MB GPU for KV entries per replica. Paste of simple bucketing logic I used:
```
# build percentiles from sample traces
percentiles = numpy.percentile(seq_lens, [50,75,90,95,99])
# map request seq to bucket index
bucket_idx = bisect_right(percentiles, req.seq_len)
# use bucket profile for kernel selection and batch shaping
```

Alin: good — that matches expectation. For prefill we should make it opt-in per deployment and gated by a memory cap. Config knobs: `autotune.bucket.strategy=percentile`, `autotune.bucket.percentiles=[50,75,90,95,99]`, `autotune.prefill.enabled=true`, `autotune.prefill.memory_cap_mb=200`.

Sam: rollout idea: canary the percentile strategy on 5% of traffic for a week, compare p99/p95, tokens/sec, and GPU mem pressure. If any regression >5% on p99, auto-roll back. Also record kernel-switch rate — if it oscillates too much we may thrash. :thinking_face:

Maya: note on oscillation: we should debounce bucket recomputation and only rebuild bucket boundaries every N minutes or when sample volume > M. Otherwise noisy traces (e.g., a big batch from a load test) could skew boundaries.

Ron: agreed. Implementation notes: keep lightweight sketch (t-digest) for percentiles to avoid full hist scans. Also track per-model-family profiles (gpt-like vs encoder-only) because seq distributions differ. Storing profiles keyed by `model@quant` is enough.

Eva: what about KV-cache prefill warmup ordering? If we prefill for top-k prefixes we might push out less-used entries. Should we combine LRU with a reuse score that decays? Also consider prefill in the background on low-priority streams to avoid head-of-line impact.

Alin: good call. Proposal: prefill uses a background `prefill` thread with `io_priority=low` and an eviction policy: `score = freq * recency_decay`. We’ll expose `autotune.prefill.background=true` and `autotune.prefill.top_k=50`.

Sam: metrics to validate: p50/p95/p99 token latency, first-token latency, kernel-launchs/sec, kernel-switch-count, gpu_mem_utilization, eviction_rate. Make them dashboards + regressions alert.

Maya: compatibility tests: run end-to-end with q4/q8 kernels, run with and without KV caching enabled, and ensure no OOMs. Add unit that asserts prefill memory < cap.

Ron: experiment plan: 1) offline simulate with trace replay to compute percentiles 2) canary percentile buckets on 5% live 3) enable prefill on a small fleet with mem cap 100MB 4) if stable, increase to 25% then full rollout. I can write the harness (should be ~200 LOC).

Alin: thanks — action items:
- Ron: prototype harness + t-digest sampler (due Wed)
- Maya: run kernel-compat matrix for q4/q8 with prefill (due Thu)
- Sam: add canary rollout config + alerts (due Fri)
- Eva: design eviction score and background prefill I/O contract (sync with Ron) (due Fri)

If nobody objects I’ll update the RFC with these notes and schedule a 30m follow-up sync next week. :thumbsup:
